dct_description_sm:
Primers were designed from 31 of the microsatellite sequences. PCR reactions were carried out in 10 mL reaction volumes containing 1x thermalase reaction buffer (100 mM Tris (pH 8.3), 500 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 0.1% Tween 20, 0.1% gelatin, 0.1% NP40), 0.1 mM dGTP, 0.1 mM dATP, 0.1 mM dTTP, 0.01 mM dCTP, 8 pmol of each primer, 1% formamide, 60 mM TMAC, 0.25 U Taq polymerase (Promega) and 0.1 mCi [a32P]-dCTP. The only exception is the reaction mix used for
locus De11 [NK buffer (67 mM Tris (pH 8), 160 mM (NH4)2SO4, 50 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl2, 0.1% Tween 20 and no TMAC or formamide]. All loci were amplified using a two-step annealing procedure: one cycle for 2 min at 94C, 45 s at TA1, 50 s at 72C; seven cycles of 50 s at 94C, 45 s at TA1, 50 s at 72C; 25 cycles of 50 s at 89C, 45 s at TA2, 50 s at 72C; and one final cycle of 5 min at 72C. The two annealing temperatures (TA1 and TA2) are specific for each primer set and listed in Burg (1999).

Blood, tissue or feather samples were collected/provided by a number of people/groups including British Antarctic Survey (Chris Hill), Deon Nel, Janet Kelso, Department of Conservation New Zealand (Jacinda Amey, Gus McAllister, Sherly Hamilton, Alan Wiltshire, Kath Walker, Graeme Elliot), Peter Moore, Henri Weimerskirch.
PCR conditions were published in Burg and Croxall 2004  https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-294X.2004.02232.x
